name: Venus Viva

lead: Venus Viva is a clinic device that delivers radiofrequency energy through tiny pins to resurface skin. People use it for smoother texture, softer acne scars and fewer wrinkles.

Fractional RF heats microscopic zones of skin through micro-pins, leaving surrounding tissue intact, which is described as shortening recovery compared with surgery or full ablation. Published work is mainly small studies, including a 20-patient acne-scar study in Indian skin (Fitzpatrick types IV-V) and a retrospective patient-satisfaction study.

paras: It is performed by clinicians in a series of sessions. Skin texture and scars improve gradually as the skin remodels over the weeks after treatment.

Fractional resurfacing generally causes redness and swelling for a period after treatment; burns and pigment change are reported RF risks. Little device-specific safety data appear in the sources reviewed.

angle.text: Venus Viva is used for smoother skin, softer acne scars and fewer wrinkles with shorter recovery than ablative approaches. Nanofractional RF micro-pins resurface the skin. Support comes from small uncontrolled studies.

lead: Venus Viva is a nanofractional radiofrequency device marketed for skin resurfacing, including acne scars and wrinkles. Fractional RF delivers thermal energy through multiple micro-pins in a targeted pattern, which is described as shortening recovery compared with surgery or full ablation [1].

Evidence consists of small studies, including a 20-patient study of nanofractional RF for acne scars in Indian skin (Fitzpatrick types IV-V) [2] and a retrospective patient-satisfaction study [1], plus a number of small registered trials of fractional RF.
infobox: Described as shorter than ablative techniques[1]

paras: Fractional RF applies energy through arrays of micro-pins rather than across the whole skin surface, which a 2015 article says avoids surgery or full ablation and hastens recovery [1].

The 2017 Indian-skin study enrolled 20 patients aged 16-60 who received one to three treatments; its authors described acne scarring as hard to treat in darker skin and nanofractional RF as shown to be effective for cosmetic improvement of acne scars [2]. A retrospective study examined patient satisfaction after a trial of nano-fractional RF [1]. Both are small and uncontrolled.

Published studies include a 20-patient acne-scar study [2] and a retrospective satisfaction study [1]. ClinicalTrials.gov lists small completed registrations of fractional RF for acne scars (n=10 to 25) [3][4], wrinkles [5], stretch marks [6] and arm tightening [7]; registry titles do not all name a specific device, and results are not summarised here.
